name: USDB Blast
oneLiner: USDB is Blast L2's native yield-bearing dollar, bridged USDC/USDT routed through MakerDAO DSR with auto-rebasing yield to Blast holders.

obituary.epitaph: The chain that issued Blast's dollar switched itself off
obituary.obituary: Blast announced on October 2, 2026 that it would wind down its Ethereum L2 because operating costs exceeded revenue, and the normal withdrawal interface closed on October 26 with about $40.4M still sitting in the canonical bridge. USDB exists only on Blast: users receive it by bridging USDC, USDT or DAI to the L2, and redeem it for DAI only by proving a withdrawal back to Ethereum, so the end of the chain ends the product even though the L1 bridge contracts still accept contract-level exits. Supply fell from about $11.4M to $8.6M in the month to capture, every tracked Blast USDB pool shows zero 24-hour volume, and CoinGecko's last quote on October 30 came from those idle pools. Pharos freezes USDB as an archived wind-down asset; holders keep the L1 bridge claim described in Blast's withdrawal guides.

collateral: DAI held through Blast's MakerDAO DSR yield manager; USDC, USDT, and DAI are supported bridge deposit inputs, while USDB withdrawals redeem to DAI.
pegMechanism: Automatic rebasing with yield from underlying centralized stablecoin strategies

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: USDB at Blast 0x4300000000000000000000000000000000000003 is an auto-rebasing protocol-position liability with an operational bridge withdrawal claim to Ethereum DAI, rather than a fiat cash claim, direct fund share or holder-created CDP. Re-fetched issuer documentation explicitly identifies DAI redemption. At Ethereum block 26099927, USDYieldManager 0xa230285d5683c74935ad14c446e137c8c8828438 retained implementation 0xecddf748a60e23609c07af6ca3856744b139b911, TOKEN()=DAI and one DSR provider 0x0733f618118bf420b6b604c969498ecf143681a8; provider index 1 reverted out-of-bounds. At Blast block 41038766, USDB bridge() and REPORTER() retained the exact L2BlastBridge and Ethereum manager. This establishes the current operational claim and model only; whole-liability reconciliation, complete position custody/continuity, encumbrance/allocation and funded default priority remain unresolved.
